newsitem.title: UK: US oil giants to develop major new Alaska oilfield.
newsitem.headline: US oil giants to develop major new Alaska oilfield.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co said on Wednesday its ARCO Alaska Inc unit, Anadarko Petroleum Corp and Union Texas Petroleum Alaska Corp planned to develop a major new oilfield in the western Colville area on Alaska's North Slope.

"A two-year delineation program, which included six wells, four sidetracks and a high-quality 3-D seismic survey, indicates that the 10-mile long, 40,000 acre oilfield has proven and potential reserves of 250 and 300 million barrels with 800 million to a billion barrels of oil in place," it said.
In a statement released in London, Atlantic said total field development was expected to cost $700 to $800 million.

Pending local, state and federal permits, field construction and development will begin in the winter of 1997/98, with initial production of 30,000 barrels of oil per day expected in early 2000 increasing to 60,000 in 2001.
Anadarko Petroleum is a Houston-based independent oil and gas exploration and production company and Union Texas is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Union Texas Petroleum Holdings.
